evidence: Plaut. Curc. 128: ingurgitat impūra in sē merum avāriter
terms.comment: The neuter of merus, pure, with vīnum understood. Wine was normally drunk with water; merum is the drinker’s word. Poetic and post-Augustan as a noun (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Hoc vidē ut ingurgitat impūra in sē merum avāriter, faucibus plēnīs.
phrases.english: Just look how the filthy creature pours neat wine into herself, greedily, by the throatful.

sources: Lewis & Short: merus
